items.title: Myra Menville Interview, 1958-05-07, 09
items.q: the neighborhood where we lived, there was the Greenmire family, the Hanes, the Downwinds, the Frelson Pages, Esperberto, and several fellas right nearby.

ctx.x: Well, what did your parents think of this whole music? And your parents...

Well, of course it didn't enter into anything at all. And when the marching parades happened, funeral parades, Negro processions happened to pass, they'd always come out and look at it, and listen with enjoyment, but with a tongue-in-cheek attitude towards it. My next real introduction to music, if you will, I had a grandmother who sang and played very well. My father, she sang and played the piano and accompanied herself. And my father played the guitar a little bit. He also played an alto horn. But when I was…
Well, what type of music did you end up playing? The popular music of the day or...?
